docs.title: General Info
docs.text:
Basic principle = get rare objects/mods/relics as fast as possible. Having a resource doubler booster helps for some farms, like relic opening or apothic plant farming.

For beginners

Mainly used for slots at the beginning of the game, the rest will come later (cosmetics, trade) The game gives you some plat at account creation, to spend in the shop: you must spend them on slots in priority. Platinum will come from trading with other players, the amount of trades per day is equal to your Mastery Rank.

Find / identify a farming method

  • find objects selling for high prices on warframe.market or in the in-game English trade chats (much more people)
  • find methods to collect these profitable objects efficiently / quickly / that you enjoy (favor cross-farms, ex: get plants for apothics while opening relics in public)
  • consult community lists 1, 2, 3, 4, 5

docs.title: Trading Places
docs.text:
• warframe.market: has the advantage of allowing to sell very quickly and continue your missions while waiting to find a buyer who will send you a message
  • trade tab in the in-game chat
    • total mess chaos. Prices vary greatly, can earn more than on market but requires more time, attention and chatting
    • prefer the English version (launcher option) + English servers (in-game connection options) to access the trade channel with the most players
    • the magnifying glass at the top left of the chat allows filtering displayed texts to avoid drowning
    • quick glossary: "WTB" = Want To Buy, "WTS" = Want To Sell
    • you can add a place by opening a bracket [ and starting to type its name and choose from auto-complete. Fast, efficient, people will know what you're selling without errors.

Final trades after contact should be preferably done in a Dojo at a trade pad. As a last resort you can go through Maroo's bazaar and use the trade emote.

docs.title: Good Deals
docs.text:
Some methods / sources, for the rest check References:

  • open relics
  • apothic mods

    Why:

    • apothic mods videos
    • drops of rare and expensive mods (Growing Power & others)

    How:

    • do Titania's quest to get apothic blueprints
    • farm plants you're interested in (see apothic ingredients)
      • Grineer Forest, Mantle (Earth, Capture)
        • Night: Dusk Saracenia, Moonlight Dragonlily, Moonlight Jadeleaf
        • Day: Sunlight Threshcone
      • Lua: Lunar Pitcher
      • Grineer Settlement, Mars on ground: Ruk's Claw
      • Grineer Asteroid, Mercury/Phobos/Saturn/Uranus: Vestan Moss
      • Corpus Outpost, Venus/Neptune/Pluto (random): Frostleaf
    • build your apothics in advance
    • form a group, 1 Khora + 3 Nekros preferably
    • run Mantle (Earth) to find Silver Grove Shrine: Lotus speaks when you enter the right tileset
    • use your loot buffs and open 2 apothics each
  • Descendia (arcanes / vosphor)

    Why: farm the "treasure rooms" stage in loop to trade resources for arcanes (arcane sales / Vosphor reroll for other arcanes)

    How:

    • do a full normal run to check rooms and unlock checkpoints for the current week
    • if a "treasure room" is well placed relative to the first 2 checkpoints, start farming:
      • use max range Xaku (+ Helminth Mag with augment mod if needed for loot)
      • enter the closest checkpoint to the treasure room
      • validate the treasure room stage, be sure to break all crates / pick up everything
      • go to the next stage and extract immediately
      • repeat (loots are saved at each stage transition)
  • corrupted mods
    • check wiki page and explanatory video
    • you will need them for your builds
    • sell the surplus for plats
    • farm on Deimos, preferably a fast map like capture on Horend
      • requires equipping corrupted keys, a random one of 4 possible is needed to open a treasure room door. Distribute keys among present players or go solo with all keys equipped
      • key blueprints are found in Dojos: join a clan and go to the Orokin lab
      • possible to do runs solo, preferably with a fast frame (Titania/Nezha)
      • recommended to do runs in group: reduces key charge and speeds up runs to find doors
  • farm Aya Cetus (group) or Deimos (Brute Force max rank solo or duo)
  • farm Captain Vor
  • farm Steel Path endurance:
    • Cascade (gdocs) + mod booster if possible (+ arcane drops)

    • Arbitration

  • Vaulted Prime parts

        • Opti Bounties on Cetus (more profitable but inaccessible for new players, reserve for groups for later)

docs.title: Method: How to do it
docs.text:
2 types of farming:

  • pure pick-up / random: open random relics without making a group in advance
    • benefits from randomly getting ally drops
    • allows you to increase your Void Trace stock to level up your "good" relics
    • favor fast missions (capture, extermination, sabotage)
  • organized group farming where everyone brings the same relic to increase specific drop chances
    • go through a community discord
    • go through the in-game recruitment channel
      • set the game to English (more people) via the launcher
      • set parameters for US servers (more people)
      • use the recruitment channel
      • click on the magnifying glass at the top left of the channel: sort by relic names you're interested in (reduces spam)
      • use in-game object links (open brackets [ ], start typing the name, use auto-complete)
      • avoid flawless relics due to low volume available (use intact for bronze loots, radiant for silver/gold loots)
      • message types:
      • H [Relic Axi V8] 2/4 rad: means Host (host/create a group) for Axi V8 relic, already 2 players out of 4, radiant relic for all ==> send him a message "+1" / "inv" to be invited
      • L [Relic Axi V8] or LF [Relic Axi V8]: means L looking for group, player alone looking for a group. Sometimes you can be contacted to create a group when sending this kind of message
      • think about keeping the menu open (escape) to keep an eye at the top left on equipped relics and be sure everyone has the right relic (and intact/radiant for all as appropriate), otherwise remake the group

docs.title: Best Spots
docs.text:
Favor maps for their speed and/or ability to combine other farms:

Lith Fissure: Bifrost Echo, Venus Proxima (Railjack)

Advantages:

  • you can invite players as soon as they have an Archwing (Mars junction quest)
  • Lith relic drops (+ pseudo-vault Nyx/Valkyr)
  • rare resource drops (Orokin Cells, Tellurium)
  • high credit drops (relative to game level)
  • Athodai drops

Strategy:

  • send a player to the "white dot" indicating a wreck (requires rank 5 in Piloting Intrinsics to see it) with a hack at the end of a corridor (bonus loot Athodai & Nyx/Valkyr relics)
  • do the very short Railjack part (destroy enemy ship with main cannon)
  • park facing / slightly above the ship entrance (easy access for all)
  • rush the extermination (AoE + fast movement, ex: Titania helminth gauss)
  • everyone must gather near the exit door (to validate mission end)
  • return to Railjack
    • avoid using Archwing
    • use Form Up to tp the whole group
    • use Omni (consumable wheel, auto-equipped in Railjack) to tp solo (requires Rank 4 in Tactical Intrinsics)

Requiem Fissure: Pago - Kuva Spy

  • follow build and strategy explained in this GazTTV video
  • high drop rate of 60/60 mods
  • high-level spy: guaranteed Meso/Neo drops
  • opening Requiem relics:
    • Requiem mod drops
    • refine to Flawless (50 traces) for optimization

Axi/Neo Fissure: capture/extermination in Void (Hepit, Ukko, Oxomoco, Teshub)

  • fast & easy missions
    • wide corridors
    • clean design: fast loading
    • each golden orb gives energy to your Prime frames
  • offers a relic at the end of each mission
    • Hepit, Teshub: Lith relic
    • Ukko, Oxomoco: Meso / Neo relic
  • popular missions: more players to advance fast and share drops

Identify good spots, use the right tools and playing in a group will be more profitable.

To identify resource sources in-game you can:

  • hover over a resource in a Foundry blueprint, the text will give you info

docs.title: Boosters
docs.text:
Very important, stacking boosters will allow you to get much more resources in the same amount of time. The resource booster (orange) is the most important, others are not worth the plat cost unless you already have a good plat income, which will come later.

Resource booster sources (increases resources from pickups):

  • companions
  • in-game shop: resource booster. Costs plats, after that slot purchase is a priority buy that will allow you to accelerate your resource farm AND your plat farm (virtuous circle). 30-day boosters are the most cost-effective in cost/day.
  • endless relics (survival, defense...) : accumulates up to +100% resource pickups

Resource drop chance boosters sources (increases resources drops on the ground):

  • farm frames
  • steel path : booster +100% drop chances
  • in-game shop : booster +100% chances de drop. Applies to whole group once. (if 4 players have it, it only applies +100% on enemies drops not 400%).
  • endless relics (survival, defense...) : accumulates up to +100% resource drop chances
  • True Master's Font, blessing from MR 30+ player in relays (go to relay to AFK / take a break and grab some blessings)

If you have no boosters do not despair. The most important is to know they exist to give you a medium-term goal to acquire them and benefit earlier.

docs.title: Fishing
docs.text:
Fishing: details

  • Gear:
    • get fishing gear (spears, baits) from Hai-Luk (Cetus), The Business (Fortuna) and Daughter (Necralisk)
    • equip your fishing spear in Arsenal, consumable wheel
    • get Luminous Dye on Cetus to see fish well
  • locations & fishing periods per fish: refer to wiki page on fishing
    • Cetus Spots
    • Fortuna Spots
  • in open-world of your choice:
    • think about using baits if needed
    • look for hotspots and use your baits if needed (purchasable from NPCs)

docs.title: Equipment
docs.text:
In your Arsenal, you can modify/improve your equipment.

Once a frame or weapon is selected you can choose to edit their characteristics by adding mods.

On the editing screen, you can see the capacity at the top left, indicating the "weight" of mods you can equip:

  • ex: 10 capacity = 1 mod at 10 capacity OR 2 mods at 5 capacity
  • all equipable items (frames, weapons, companions, archwings etc) occupy a limited slot. You can buy more, but it will cost platinum
  • the base capacity of equipment increases with your account Mastery level, playing with a given item increases its mastery and thus its capacity
  • You can quickly increase a frame or weapon capacity by equipping respectively an aura (ex: Dreamer's Bond) and a stance (ex: Swooping Falcon for Skana)
  • The cost in credits and Endo to level up mods is exponential, it depends on:
    • the "rarity / quality" of the mod, the higher it is, the more expensive: bronze, silver, gold, primed/galvanized/archon
    • the number of ranks: the cost is exponential. For a rank 10 mod, avoid maxing it directly to balance investment and return when you have few resources (ex: having 3 mods rank 7 is better than one mod rank 10)

docs.title: Mods: General Info
docs.text:
Mods make you stronger

Leveling up your mods is the ABCs of becoming more resistant and dealing more damage.

  • fusion (leveling up) your mods makes your mods even more effective: it's better to have 2 leveled mods that take 15 capacity and give lots of stats than 6 mods that occupy the same with almost no effect.
  • requires Endo and credits to level up your mods (see Farm), upgrade cost depends
    • on the quality of mods. The more they are "shiny" (bronze > silver > gold > primed/galvanized/archon), the more expensive it will be
    • on the number of ranks: the more you progress, the more expensive the upgrade per rank
      • it will be better in the beginning to avoid max ranks and level several mods to an intermediate rank to achieve a good compromise. Ex: Level 3 mods at rank 7/10 instead of one at 10/10.
  • mod slots can be polarized: they have a specific mod sign ("V" "D" "-" etc) indicating they are specialized for a mod family/polarity:
    • reduces the capacity cost of mods from the same family (divided by 2, shown in green)
    • increases the capacity cost of mods from other families (shown in red)

docs.title: Loadouts
docs.text:
The first line at the top left of the Arsenal corresponds to presets/loadouts: you can save a setup corresponding to given equipment (a frame, 3 weapons, a pet with specific mods).

You can make different loadouts, for example:

  • one for Volt oriented towards melee weapons to quickly finish missions
  • another for Volt oriented towards nuking by dealing lots of damage with ability 4
  • another with Rhino for tanking in more difficult missions
  • etc...

Note that you can select prepared loadouts on the fly in your navigation, to adapt your tools according to your desires or game modes.

docs.title: Warframes
docs.text:
Warframe mods have 2 main purposes:

  • base stats: mainly survivability
  • powers/abilities:
    • enhanced: power boost for better buffs / nukes, better range, etc...
    • modified: augment mods that will change the behavior of certain abilities. Ex: the mod allows Frost to tank much better.

You will also find some utility mods (cast speed, parkour speed).

Remember to hover with your cursor over the different stats on the left, this will give you details on their actual impact.

Also remember to hover over passive and ability icons below stats to see the impact of your mods on them.

docs.title: Warframe Mods: Base Stats
docs.text:
• Health / Armor: base combo, increasing health increases your survival and armor reduces damage taken by health points
  • Shields: additional "tanking" bar. 50% innate damage reduction, automatically recharges after a certain time. When shields reach 0, you get an invulnerability period called "shield-gating"
  • Energy: the fuel for all your abilities. Increasing the max pool will give you more comfort.
  • Sprint Speed: not much to say, you will move quickly via maneuvers like the roll and bullet-jump which benefit from another stat: velocity.

docs.title: Warframe Mods: Powers
docs.text:
• Duration: for controls (longer) and buffs (long duration = less energy spent and more comfort)
  • Efficiency: reduces ability cost, big gameplay comfort
  • Range: useful mainly for controls or AoE nukes, less useful if you focus on weapon damage buffs
  • Power: generally for hitting harder, sometimes for increasing buffs and heals

docs.title: Damage: Essential Stats
docs.text:
Identify the best synergies for your weapons and stack multipliers.

base damage formula

base damage X elemental damage X crit chance X crit damage

Remember to hover your cursor over the different stats on the left to understand their details, especially status stats corresponding to infused status.

  • base damage: increases all weapon damage (Serrated, Barrel, Pressure Points), stat that will be multiplied by many other mods. Mandatory.
  • elemental damage
    • multiplies base damage
    • putting two status together merges them to give a combined status
    • the game reads mod slots from left to right and top to bottom like a book: arrange mods in this order to get desired combinations
      • example 1: "toxin + electricity + fire" will give "corrosive (tox + elec) + fire"
      • example 2: "fire + toxin + electricity" will give "gas (fire + tox) + electricity"
    • enemies have different positive/negative resistances to damage, ex:
      • corrosive (toxin + electricity) deals +50% damage to Grineer
      • toxin ignores shields and attacks health directly. Very effective against Corpus which have little health and lots of shields.
    • gives access to elements sometimes having important effects for damage:
      • viral (toxin + cold): increases damage to health by 100 to 325% (10 stacks max per target for max effect)
      • magnetic (cold + electricity): increases damage to shields and overguard (Eximus, Thrax) by 100 to 325%, 10 stacks
      • corrosive (toxin + electricity): reduces enemy armor by 26 to 80% at 10 stacks. Possibility to increase stacks later via archon shards
      • heat: deals damage over time per stack + reduces armor by 15 to 50% (max effect after 5s of burn). No max stacks, increases as long as it's applied
  • crit chance
    • increases chances of critical hit multiplying base and elemental damage
    • can exceed 100% for big crits (orange) or even super crits (red+). We talk about "crit tiers".
    • mods increase the weapon's base crit stats. A weapon with low crit (<20% or so) benefits little from crit mods
  • crit damage: multiplier applied to crits to make them even more massive

status choice

  • if in doubt for status to use, start with Viral + Heat or Corro + Heat (big generalization but it works)
  • for more details consult this video explaining status and their strengths

Sometimes weapons have high status chance and/or low crits, you can then focus on another stat:

  • status chance
    • increases status chance. Can exceed 100% (gives additional procs)
    • different types of status effects:
    • debuff:
      • damage received debuff: viral, magnetic
      • stat debuff (armor, other): corrosive, heat, cold, puncture
      • CC debuff (crowd control): cold, radiation, heat, electricity, impact, blast
    • damage over time (DoT): heat, electricity, toxin, gas, blast, slash

docs.title: Primary & Secondary Weapons
docs.text:
Some stats are exclusive to primary/secondary weapons:

  • multishot: increases the number of bullets fired per shot. Multiplies all other damage stats
    • Primaries: Split Chamber
    • Secondaries: Barrel Diffusion + Lethal Torrent
  • fire rate: rate of fire, allows increasing DPS at the cost of worse ammo economy

docs.title: CO: Condition Overload, GunCO
docs.text:
Big damage boost potential

We talk about CO for all mechanics similar to Condition Overload mod: mods giving a damage bonus based on the amount of different status present on a target.

Affected mods: Condition Overload, Galvanized Aptitude, Galvanized Shot, Galvanized Savvy + some weapon passives (Incarnon mainly).

  • by default the damage bonus from these mods is additive with your base damage
  • in some cases the bonus from these mods is multiplicative with your base damage

Outside of the classic use with a primer which works well with the default functionality, very high damage can be achieved when the weapon works multiplicatively with this mod.

If you don't have the faith to test each weapon to see which category it falls into, consult the community GunCO sheet.

docs.title: Melee Weapons
docs.text:
The same base logic applies: "base damage X elemental damage X crit chance X crit damage".

Melee Stats Synergy

base damage X elemental damage X attack speed/range X crit chance X crit damage

  • melee scaling mods:
    • priority: Blood Rush, Weeping Wounds, Condition Overload
    • others: to a lesser extent Gladiator Set (we like Gladiator Might but it's often outclassed by Galvanized Steel)
  • check if the weapon already has high base status % or crit % and mod accordingly (boosting a low value is not interesting)
  • stance:
    • adds capacity like frame auras
    • allows varying attacks and combos as well as damage dealt by combos (some stances are more enjoyable to play and/or hit harder, for example Sovereign Outcast which dominates tonfas)
  • attack speed: Fury, Quickening & Berserker Fury are affordable
  • range: (Primed) Reach, allows hitting enemies from further / more enemies at once

docs.title: Glaive Weapons
docs.text:
Glaives are very special melee weapons. You throw them with a heavy attack and can make them explode at distance with a heavy/secondary attack.

From Mastery Rank 4 you can obtain a Xoris which is an excellent glaive.

Mods used on them are quite particular:

  • gain combo via Corrupt Charge to increase explosion damage
  • specific mods for explosion:
    • Volatile Quick Return for a single explosion with great range (very common)
    • Volatile Rebound for an explosion on each bounce (especially for Falcor glaive)
    • mods that do NOT affect explosion: range, attack speed

docs.title: Weapon Mods: Survival
docs.text:
Uncommon, survival sources in weapons can complement a setup/loadout too fragile otherwise (ex: frame completely oriented towards damage buff)

  • Arcane Secondary Fortifier:
    • allows secondary weapons to steal up to 15,000 overguard from enemies for your frame
    • lots of Eximus with overguard in Steel Path = ideal situation for this arcane
    • very good synergy with status DoT weapons (damage over time) and/or AoE weapons (area of effect), ex: Furis Incarnon, Akarius Prime, Kuva Nukor, Dual Toxocyst incarnon
  • Rakta Dark Dagger: generates shields when attacking irradiated enemies (weapon has base radiation). Good in pure electric influence, elec/blast, elec/gas builds. Passive doesn't work at 0 shields, sometimes need to generate some by choosing from the following solutions:
    • Brief Respite
    • Augur mods
    • Fast Deflection + Vigilante Vigor
    • bonus: being a dagger, works well with Amalgam Argonak to add armor strip to the weapon
  • Energizing Shot + secondary weapon + shoot an energy orb + Equilibrium / purple shard = instant self-revive
  • if needed add Protea specter / Kuva Zarr crewmate to generate orbs
  • if needed equip Undying Will
  • Arcane Reaper:
    • max rank: +660 armor / +24 hp/sec for 10s. Can stack multiple times
    • niche: requires a healthtank build + a weapon that already overkills without arcane (ex: Valkyr claws). Will prefer influence or arcane exposure most of the time

docs.title: Anti-acolyte Strategies
docs.text:
Video with the essential info.

The acolyte damage reduction formula can be found on the wiki, it is calculated based on a DPS metric dependent on the firerate sustained. No firerate, less damage reduction.

To mitigate the impact of acolyte damage reduction:

  • avoid attacking them with a weapon having a lot of firerate/multishot (simple bullets/projectiles or beam/continuous attack)
  • prioritize high critical tiers (100+ crit chance) which allow to partially ignore the attenuation
  • prioritize large damage instances in few hits
  • prioritize AoE projectile weapons (different calculation)
  • prioritize melee weapons if possible (ignore firerate/multishot part as they have none)

Utility pets: double-loot, energy, CC

docs.title: Steel Path Warframes
docs.text:
Focus on a very small pool of warframes at the beginning, preferably with good built-in survival tools without too much investment.

Force yourself to read the full descriptions of the frame's kit (Arsenal > Hover over Frame > Abilities: read passive, abilities and all tips).

Consider adding a Helminth for damage or survival.

docs.title: RECOMMENDED FRAMES
docs.text:
The selection is already reduced, to push further the top prio / super-meta / easy are indicated in bold:

Prio: autonomous damage & status resistance

Dante, Revenant, Kullervo, Follie

Nezha, Rhino, Valkyr, Trinity, Gauss, Atlas, Uriel

Very good: damage resistance + need to add status resistance

  • add status resistance externally:
    • Nova, Protea, Wisp, Baruuk, Hildryn, Ash, Citrine, Nyx, Yareli, Xaku, Octavia
  • special case: Lavos (passive + Synth Fiber to remove cooldown)

Bonus choices

  • Rush Spy/Capture: Wukong, Titania, Voruna (bonus velocity)
  • Weapon platform: Saryn, Mirage, Volt, Oraxia
  • others: in principle all frames are viable, those listed can just make Steel Path access easier and are less demanding than others in terms of survival/DPS/modding.

docs.title: FRAME MODS: SURVIVE
docs.text:
• health, armor & Adaptation mod:
    • without arcane: for early Steel Path this can help pass a threshold. Damage reduction skills can also help. After that it peters out (lvl 1500+ in endless missions) but that's not a problem here.
    • with Arcane Persistence: health/armor tanking viable at lvl cap. Prerequisites:
      • minimum 700 armor for activation. Count 1400 armor to handle heat or corrosive procs (1892 for proc+corro at same time but very rare). Consider blue archon shards.
      • take into account magnetic status and nullifiers that can disable the arcane (!):
        • status: either use cleanses (Saryn's Molt, Rolling Guard mod), or status immunity (Inaros' Scarab Armor, Trinity's Link, Titania's Helminth Spellbind / Trinity's Well of Life, etc...)
        • nullifiers: have enough AoE or melee weapons with lots of range and/or impact status. Consider a fast-firing weapon or one that can cancel shields (Miter with Neutralizing Justice)
  • Shieldgating:
    • Catalyzing Shields + Brief Respite / Augur mods: active/dynamic gameplay and energy-demanding, so need good management (Flow + Equilibrium and/or little Efficiency and/or Helminth Nourish from Grendel, for example)
    • Primed Redirection + Guardian (companion mod): expensive technique, complements with Vigilante Vigor + Fast Deflection or even Arcane Aegis if you want to push it. For the companion with Guardian, prefer a Diriga (Arc Coil + Guardian + Manifold Bond + Momentous Bond + (Primed) Regen, NO Assault Mode) and a weapon full of status (Prime Laser Rifle + Viral/Fire/Mag/Rad)
    • Omamori (Helminth) + Catalyzing Shields + Vigilante Vigor + Fast Deflection +/- Arcane Aegis: quasi-invulnerability passive as long as Omamori is maintained
  • Invisibility: very strong but sensitive to stray bullets (bad positioning) and damage over time (Rolling Guard compensates)
    • Frame ability: Ash, Ivara, Loki, Octavia, Oraxia, Voruna, Wisp, Wukong, Cyte-09
    • Helminth:
      • Evade from Cyte, little compatible with group play
      • Quiver from Ivara, reserved for static or haphazard gameplay (possible to plant the arrow in your sentinel)
    • Companions: for "caster" frames that don't need to use weapons (Protea, Xaku, Dante...)
      • Shade Prime: more solid (less aggro), access to Guardian mod
      • Huras Kubrow: free companion that can die more easily, gives access to retriever mods + Kubrow nuke

docs.title: ENERGY
docs.text:
In most cases, running out of energy is synonymous with death: either you no longer kill dangerous enemies, or you no longer cast skills to feed shieldgating.

Two main strategies that can be combined:

  • reduce the cost of skills:
  • efficiency: direct reduction
    • Arcane Sculptor
      • frame (very) compatible: Cyte, Follie, Gara, Gyre, Jade, Protea, Vauban, Volt
      • helminth (very) compatible: Brightbonnet (Nokko), Molt (Saryn), Astral Shell (Sirius & Orion)
  • duration: for buffs, fewer casts / minute => less energy spent
  • increase the stock/energy pool and ways to refill it
  • energy pool: Flow, Primed Flow, blue archon shards (2-3 max)
  • energy supply:
    • common / meta:
      • drop + conversion health orbs: companion AoE + Synth Deconstruct + health > energy conversion (Equilibrium, purple shards)
      • helminth skill:
        • Nourish from Grendel, combo possible with Energy Nexus and/or Archon Stretch (proc with Arc Coil from Diriga or elec on companion claws)
        • Brightbonnet from Nokko. The rebound of the projectile from the skill or frame on the mushrooms created allows speeding up energy regeneration. Think about "spamming" against a wall to make it rebound on mushrooms very quickly. Excellent combo with Arcane Sculptor.
      • Arcane Energize most expensive/difficult to farm today but very effective (prioritize reroll Vosfor, event drops or plats... Eidolon runs as last resort)
      • kill an Eximus: guaranteed energy orb drop
      • Large Energy Restore ("pizza"): bind to a shortcut in the consumable wheel + keyboard/gamepad shortcut. Can be spammed in normal, cooldown in SP. x100 craft blueprint available in Dojo.
    • uncommon:
      • archon shard yellow: +50% efficiency on energy orbs (+75% for tau-forged)
      • Parazon: make a finisher with Blood for Energy
      • Non-Helminth Skills
      • Duplex Bond + companion that hits hard in melee
      • Focus school Zenurik Energy Pulse (incompatible with certain game modes requiring Madurai)
      • Arcane Primary Exhilarate on main weapon primer (ex: Bubonico with forced impact + AoE)
      • Arcane Emergence Dissipate for operator
      • Energy Generator from Dethcube companion
      • Xata Invocation from the Grimoire (secondary weapon)
      • Rage / Hunter Adrenaline: losing health often means getting one-shot at a certain point in Steel Path, avoid except in special cases
      • Entropy effect from Cephalon Suda faction: passively by gaining XP while carrying weapons/mods with the effect, generates 25% max energy for 30s and gives 25% energy. Notably Entropy Burst from Supra Vandal which can make a energy regen rifle and anti-nullifier shield weapon thanks to high firerate.

docs.title: HELMINTH
docs.text: Unlock Helminth on Deimos to apply abilities to other frames and free up frame slots without uselessly "throwing away" them.

docs.title: Priority Helminth Abilities
docs.text:
Very strong, common & meta:

  • damage (stat buffs):
    • Roar from Rhino to boost anti-faction, synergizes with damage over time (fire, blast, toxin, elec)
    • Xata from Xaku to add Void damage (many interactions + Void bonus damage on overguard + magnetic bubble effect)
    • Nourish from Grendel to boost energy gain, Viral bonus, light CC
    • Wrathful Advance from Kullervo to buff melee crit %, reverse the cast via preferences and aim at the ground
  • tanking:
    • Pillage from Hildryn for shield gain + armor/shield strip + cleanse status
    • Omamori from Koumei for pseudo-dodge (very strong in addition to dodge/shield-gating)
  • armor strip: less priority today, makes enemies more fragile:
    • Pillage from Hildryn, shield and armor strip, requires lots of power (rather with Corrosive Projection aura) + blocked by walls, long cast
    • Terrify from Nekros, armor only, no LoS, requires little power, fast cast, costs quite a lot of energy
    • Tharros Strike from Styanax, armor and shield strip, LoS, fast cast, heals health, short range
    • Ophanim Eyes from Jade, armor only, continuous debuff in vision cone, little energy consumed + enemy slow

docs.title: Niche Helminth Abilities
docs.text:
Sometimes useful, much less visible/prevalent:

  • damage (stat buffs):
    • Eclipse: increases base damage (like a Serration mod). Heavily nerfed in the past, can be useful. Multiplicative damage buff applied after the rest. Double bonus for melee projectiles (Exodia Contagion, Glaives)
    • Thermal Sunder from Gauss + augment mod Thermal Transfer to add Blast
    • Shock from Volt + Shock Trooper: electric damage boost
    • Warcry from Valkyr: melee attack speed buff (mostly) and armor (a bit)
    • Breach Surge from Wisp: multiplies damage received from one target to inflict on another, light CC (radiation + blind, does not affect Eximus)
    • Airburst from Zephyr + Airbust Rounds: secondary weapon damage buff, requires hitting many targets (range) often an anti-synergy
  • damage (debuff):
    • Webbed Embrace from Oraxia: zone CC (3 zones max) + vulnerability debuff (= increased damage received)
    • Sentient Wrath from Caliban: cone CC + vulnerability debuff
    • Rest & Rage from Equinox (Day version, requires a clear emission color on the frame): enemy speed boost + vulnerability debuff
  • tanking:
  • buff / frame effect:
    • Molt from Saryn: light aggro (instant part), speed boost, status cleanse & instant cast (useful for shield-gating)
    • Null Star from Nova: 75% DR + enemy CC
    • Condemn from Harrow: shield regen + enemy CC + easy headshots
    • Quiver from Ivara, allows creating static invisibility zones. Very particular gameplay. Possibility to link the zone to a sentinel, hard to achieve consistently in dangerous situations
    • Eclipse: 75% damage reduction. Can be shared with allies via Total Eclipse
  • enemy control:
    • Resonator from Octavia, completely disables enemy AI. Requires lots of range
    • Astral Shell from Sirius & Orion: automatically generates when hit invulnerable decoys that draw fire to them within 30m. Couple with a bit of shield regen. Compatible with Arcane Sculptor
    • Silence from Banshee: disables enemy abilities (including Eximus auras) + short stun
    • Shooting Gallery from Mesa + Muzzle Flash: very good CC but no longer affects Eximus, small damage buff too
    • Gloom from Sevagoth, important slow + life steal, big energy drain
    • Webbed Embrace from Oraxia: zone CC (3 zones max) + vulnerability debuff (= increased damage received)
  • energy: (other than Nourish...)
    • Dispensary from Protea: generation of health/energy orbs + ammo at a fixed point
    • Fractured Blast from Citrine for health/energy orb generation
    • Lycath's Hunt from Voruna for health orb generation on melee attacks / energy on headshots (use Equilibrium + melee)

docs.title: STATUS RESISTANCE
docs.text:
Status from enemies has 3 main dangers:

  • damage over time: especially toxin, fire, slash
  • controls: the most annoying are Knockdown and Stagger blocking you in place
  • energy drain via Magnetic status, less common but potentially deadly

You can protect yourself in different ways via immunities or cleanses/removals. Requires specific frame kits or external sources (Helminth, mods, companions, arcanes).

Control Immunity:

  • Not mandatory, strongly recommended. In Steel Path there are + more Eximus and a greater density of mobs: + dangerous controls. Being immune prevents dying while a mob knocks you down without being able to react
  • Have a frame immunized via skills or Overguard (see recommended frames)
  • Use Primed Sure Footed or Handspring for controls
  • avoid Sure Footed (non-prime)
  • if PSF impossible, prefer Handspring, only takes one mod
  • Sure Footed (non-prime) + Fortitude possible for 100% immunity but takes one slot and "breaks" your builds, rarely feasible (unless survival already based on passive shield regen)
  • Negate from Wyrm in combo with Manifold Bond to reduce cooldown. Requires being very comfortable with DPS and being able to keep your companion alive / bring it back quickly (Momentous Bond + Primed Regen and others)

docs.title: AUGMENT MODS
docs.text:
Also called syndicate mods.

  • Easy access: leveling syndicates happens passively, you can trade the most requested augments from your syndicates for other mods or for plat and buy the mods you're missing.
  • Very variable utility: between "mandatory / hyper OP" and "meh".
  • notable augments (prio / super-meta indicated in bold, Helminth compatibility with a * star):

    • Khora: Pilfering Strangledome
    • Nekros: Despoil

docs.title: MOBILITY
docs.text:
Maneuvers are the basis of Warframe movement: bullet-jumps, rolls, slides... reference video

Fundamental part of the game for:

  • the fun of the game
  • movement speed
  • survivability
  • the roll provides 75% damage reduction, or even invulnerability via Rolling Guard
  • fast movement greatly reduces the probability of being hit / enemy accuracy
  • Survival Instinct from Sly Vulpaphyla even resets enemy targeting AI every 5 seconds via a bullet jump

Common sources:

  • Velocity: major impact, increases bullet-jump and roll distances
    • Praedos: 30% (+speed boost)
    • Archon shard yellow: +15 / +22.5%
    • velocity mods: relatively niche, can replace PSF in exilus on some builds if you have invulnerability or are comfortable
    • exilus Proton Pulse for experienced Cascade players
    • arcanes (more rare) Agility & Consequence
  • Sprint Speed
    • Praedos +20% (OK + velocity speed boost)
    • Innodem / Okina incarnon: +30% (max for melee)
    • exilus melee: Dispatch Overdrive: +60% after heavy attack (mostly slam builds)
    • Amalgam Serration: for main weapon
    • Helminth: Molt: multiple uses with status cleanse + speed + instant energy spending for shieldgating
  • Dodge Speed: only one source, Amalgam Barrel Diffusion on secondary weapon
  • Slide: minor impact

docs.title: Lich Weapons
docs.text:
Many possible weapons, some more fun than others. 3 different types of Liches currently:

  • Grineer: Kuva Lich
  • Corpus: Sister of Parvos
  • Infested: Technocyte Coda

checklist MANDATORY prerequisites to get a Lich

  • be MR 5 (since Update 35 of 2023)
  • have done War Within + Rising Tide
  • not have an active lich (only one at a time)
    • to check: go in game menu and see bottom right if you have a red/blue/green button next to your Nightwave

Displayed MR requirement vs real

There are 2 types of Lich weapons:

  • Lich weapons obtained from Foundry after battle (Kuva + Tenet)
    • ignore MR requirements, only need MR 5 + War Within + Rising Tide
  • Lich weapons obtained from in-game shops with tokens (Coda weapons + Tenet from Ergo Glast)
    • follow normal MR requirement rules to obtain the weapon
      • at MR 16 you have unlocked all Tenet from Ergo Glast (MR 14 to 16 depending on weapons)
      • at MR 17 you have unlocked all Coda from Eleanor (MR 17 for all)

docs.title: Status / Progenitors
docs.text: Lich weapons benefit from a damage/status bonus from +20 to +60%, whose status is determined by the frame that generated the Lich (larva, candidate...). We call this frame the progenitor.

docs.title: Status Types
docs.text:
See Progenitor list for details. Example: use Saryn for a toxin weapon, Nezha for a fire weapon, Mesa for a magnetic weapon.

These status are less critical to create a weapon than in the past: they can be changed with an Elemental Vice.

Optimal Status: Kuva / Tenet

See the list of recommended status.

Optimal Status: Coda

Can change according to meta/knowledge state, just for reference:

  • primaries:
    • Bassocyst: Cold/Fire (make Blast)
    • Hema: Magnetic
    • Sporothrix: Elec (goal: Blast + Elec)
    • Synapse: Fire (goal: Corro / Blast or Corro/Fire)
  • secondaries:
    • Tysis: Magnetic
    • Pox: Cold (goal: Corro / Blast with Primed Heated Charge)

  • melee:

docs.title: Priming
docs.text:
Priming consists of "preparing" enemies with a status source so that another damage weapon benefiting from this status can destroy it even more powerfully just after. Big damage boost potential, can help pass a threshold (Steel Path trash mobs, mini-bosses like Demolysts in Disruption).

Also see interaction with CO / GunCO mods (condition overload/status overload, Galvanized Shot, Galvanized Aptitude).
